title: Most scans come back without a real shop price, so the verdict reads like a guess and shoppers stop opening the app
evidence: NOW.md 2026-11-14/15: 'Only 27% of 176 real scans had a shop price.' Live /api/attribution (2026-11-21): Open Prices 874 observations on 417 barcodes; Project Hammer 47,404 barcodes; Statistics Canada 110 staples. The typed path's no-price sentence is 'Pexi does not have a price for that yet. Scan the barcode instead.' (app/server.ts:1139), which sends the shopper to the counted scan.
fix: Set a launch gate on the share of real scans that get a shop price (for example half), measured weekly from the scan log, and fill the most-scanned unpriced barcodes first.
fix_cost: days to weeks of data work; the measurement is an hour

title: Shoppers outside Toronto get verdicts built on one Toronto neighbourhood's prices and see them as wrong
evidence: Live /api/attribution: Project Hammer, the largest store-price source, is 'collected by Project Hammer for one Toronto neighbourhood: 98,918 price observations'. BC liquor prices are BC only. Statistics Canada is the only provincial source and covers 110 products. The listing sells it as 'judged against typical prices in Canada'.
fix: Either launch the marketing in the Toronto area first, or scale Toronto prices by the Statistics Canada province ratio and say on the answer which city the price comes from.
fix_cost: 1 to 2 days for the province adjustment; zero for a Toronto-first launch

title: The free tier gives away the core product: typed searches are free and uncounted, so almost nobody needs Pexi Plus
evidence: Live Terms of Use s.8: 'Typed searches are free and are not counted.' RULINGS 'Shin Plus pricing and free scans' keeps this. Plus sells only more barcode scans (10 to 100 a week). Effect on conversion is assumed, the rule itself is checked.
fix: Decide what Plus gives that free does not (unlimited scans plus something shoppers value, such as watch-list price alerts), or count typed lookups that return a verdict.
fix_cost: an hour of decision, then store text and a small server change

title: The 10-scan weekly wall lands in the middle of one shopping trip, so the first paywall a shopper sees feels like a trap
evidence: docs/decisions.md (break-even section): 'nobody knows yet how many scans one shop visit takes ... If a typical visit needs more than 5, the limit stops people in the middle of a shop'. NOW.md: 176 real scans in total, so scans per visit was never measured.
fix: Count scans per store visit from the beta log before launch; if a visit is often above 10, make the free allowance per visit or per day instead of per week.

title: Pexi is down while the shopper stands in the aisle
evidence: Commit 4786ec6: the Mac 'ran flat 2026-11-18, Pexi down 2 hours'. Live /api/health 2026-11-21: mac_on_battery (80% left), backup job failed its last run, disk and integrity jobs stale. Listing: 'Pexi needs an internet connection to answer.'
fix: Keep the server on mains power with a small UPS now, and move it to a cloud machine before the founder's job starts.
fix_cost: UPS about CA$100; cloud machine about CA$10 to 30 a month plus a day of moving

title: Typed search puts bare rows with no size or brand first, so the verdict compares the wrong pack
evidence: Live /api/search?q=kraft dinner: first candidate 0068100145120 'Kraft dinner' with brands null and quantity null, ahead of sized rows. 'lait 2%': first two candidates have no size. A shelf price cannot be judged without a size.
fix: Rank rows that carry a size and brand above bare rows of the same name, and hide a bare duplicate when a sized one exists.

title: The reviewer opens Pexi Plus and the purchase fails, because no purchase was ever completed against the store
evidence: docs/paywall-go-live-2026-11-17.md: paywall 'built, never run against a real store'; Stage 4 sandbox purchase not run (NOW.md 2026-11-17: 'Paywall purchase ... still not run'). NOW.md 2026-11-18: the free limit is ON live 'ahead of Stage 4', against RULINGS 'Both switch on only once a test purchase works end to end'. Apple's submitting page: Apple reviews 'Apple In-App Purchases' as part of a submission.
fix: Run Stage 4 (sandbox buy, reinstall, restore) on the current build, submit both subscription products with the binary, and unset the limit until it passes.
fix_cost: about an hour of Aurik's phone time

title: Review is rejected under 2.1 because the server is unreachable or answers nothing during review
evidence: Apple Review Guidelines 2.1: 'Enable backend services so that they're live and accessible during review.' Live health shows the Mac on battery and failing jobs; mac/10-boot-survival.sh says an unplanned restart 'stops at the unlock screen until a password is entered'. The drafted review notes say 'If it ever shows no answer, please retry in a few minutes', which tells the reviewer to expect failure.
fix: For the review window keep the Mac on mains with alerts on, and drop the 'retry in a few minutes' sentence from the review notes.

title: Permission text promises photographing items, a feature that does not ship
evidence: native/ios/App/App/Info.plist NSCameraUsageDescription: 'scan barcodes and photograph items'; NSPhotoLibraryUsageDescription and NSPhotoLibraryAddUsageDescription are present. RULINGS: 'photo scanning is not a shipped feature'. Guideline 2.3 asks metadata to 'accurately reflect the app's core experience'.
fix: Reword the camera text to barcodes and shelf-tag text only; drop the photo library keys and the camera plugin if nothing calls them.

title: The privacy manifest declares fewer data types than the store privacy label
evidence: PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy lists DeviceID, ProductInteraction, SearchHistory and OtherUserContent. docs/store/listing.md privacy table also declares Coarse Location, Purchase History and Other Diagnostic Data. Apple's submitting page: privacy details include 'the practices of third-party partners whose code you integrate'.
fix: Add the three missing types to the manifest so the privacy report and the label agree.

title: Age rating answered None for alcohol while 7,555 BC liquor products can be named
evidence: docs/store/listing.md age-rating table: 'None' for alcohol references, and its own note that 'the worst outcome is a rejection asking for 13+'. Live /api/attribution: BC liquor list, 7,555 barcodes.
fix: Answer 'Infrequent' up front (13+) to skip a resubmission round, or keep None and accept the risk.

title: Money arrives before GST/HST, business-name registration and the Terms redraft are settled
evidence: docs/paywall-go-live-2026-11-17.md Stage 3: 'Before real money ... GST/HST registration and Form GST506 to Apple, Ontario business name, Terms s.11/s.12 redraft'. docs/security-legal-check-plan-2026-11-16.md:203-204: 'To confirm: whether Apple collects and remits GST/HST on Canadian App Store sales'. Nothing in NOW.md says these are done.
fix: Confirm Apple's GST/HST role on Canadian app sales with CRA's digital economy guidance, register the Ontario business name 'Pexi', and finish the Terms redraft before the first paid sale.

title: Every claim, dispute or breach lands on the founder personally
evidence: Live Terms s.1 and privacy policy: 'Pexi is published by Jamin Xu, an individual developer', who is also named the person in charge under Quebec's privacy law. docs/the-store-accounts-packet.md:68: 'There is no incorporated entity'. The server records every tap and search (privacy policy) on one laptop at home.
fix: Incorporate before marketing spend, or at least before the job starts, and keep only the data the product uses.

title: No written agreement with Aurik on who owns the code and how money splits
evidence: A grep of RULINGS.md and docs/decisions.md for agreement, equity, split, shareholder and partnership found nothing beyond the work split ('Who owns what'). Aurik holds Maintainer access and wrote the paywall and screens. Absence in the repo is not proof of absence; whether copyright in his code transfers without an assignment is assumed, not checked.
fix: One-page founders' agreement: IP assignment to the publisher, revenue split, what happens if either leaves.
fix_cost: an evening, or about CA$500 for a lawyer's read

title: The full-time employer's contract claims or bars a side app
evidence: Not checked: the founder's employment documents were not opened by design. Employment contracts often carry IP assignment and outside-activity clauses; this is an assumption, not a finding about his contract.
fix: Read the IP and outside-work clauses and get written OK for Pexi before the start date.

title: A stolen or lost MacBook exposes every shopper record, and disk encryption may not be on
evidence: mac/10-boot-survival.sh:28: 'What this does NOT do: turn FileVault on (it needs Jamin's password ...)'. The repo shows no check that it was turned on. The server holds device ids, IP addresses, search text and coarse location (privacy policy). Quebec's privacy law makes a breach reportable.
fix: Run 'fdesetup status' on the Mac and record the result; if off, turn it on (and see the founder seat on remote unlock).

title: Apple keeps 30% instead of 15% if the Small Business Program is not joined
evidence: docs/decisions.md:2948: monthly nets 'US$2.44 at 15% (Small Business Program) or US$2.01 at 30%'. No record in NOW.md that enrolment was done.
fix: Enrol in the App Store Small Business Program before the first sale.

title: Once the job starts, an outage lasts until the founder gets home and types a password
evidence: mac/10-boot-survival.sh:15-22: with FileVault an unplanned restart 'stops at the unlock screen until a password is entered'; unlock over SSH 'works from the LAN only'. Commit 4786ec6: battery ran flat 2026-11-18, 2 hours down. Live health today: on battery at 80%.
fix: Move the server to a cloud machine (or a mains-powered Mac mini with a UPS and remote unlock) before May 2027.
fix_cost: about CA$10 to 30 a month and 1 to 2 days

title: Alarms fire and nobody acts on them
evidence: Live /api/health 2026-11-21: 'The Mac job backup failed its last run', disk and integrity jobs 'not reported within its period', Mac on battery. The watch exists (app/src/watch.ts, Healthchecks ping) yet the problems stand at the time of the probe.
fix: Send each watch problem as a phone push that repeats until cleared, with Aurik as second contact.

title: Only the founder can run the backend, the accounts and the store listing
evidence: RULINGS 'Who owns what': Jamin owns 'the server, the catalogue, prices and every database, the Mac (deploys, settings and keys, backups, power), the accounts and the store listing ... building and uploading the app, and the submission'. Aurik owns the app only.
fix: A one-page runbook (restart, deploy, unlock, renew) and give Aurik the access to do each step.

title: The server's domain lapses mid-job
evidence: The app's server is relay.anjiawenda.com (CLAUDE.md, Beta data). Verisign RDAP 2026-11-21: anjiawenda.com 'expiration: 2027-08-20'. Auto-renew state not visible.
fix: Turn on auto-renew and add years now.

title: Launched with no proof anyone will pay
evidence: NOW.md: 176 real scans in all; no purchase ever completed. docs/decisions.md names the falsifier 'under 1 in 10 testers who reach the limit tap Subscribe' and it was never measured.
fix: Set a two-week number after launch (paywall views to subscribe taps) and a continue or stop call against it.

title: Updates stop after April 2027 because the build Mac lacks the new SDK
evidence: Apple's submitting page: 'Starting April 2027 ... iOS and iPadOS apps must be built with the iOS & iPadOS 27 SDK or later'. The same Mac builds the app and runs the server, so an Xcode or macOS update means a planned restart of production.
fix: Plan the Xcode upgrade with the planned-restart script before April, or move building off the server Mac.

title: The upkeep of the rule system outlasts the founder's evenings
evidence: RULINGS.md is 95 KB, the repo CLAUDE.md 18.7 KB; every bug runs a multi-step fix loop with claims and two remotes (CLAUDE.md). Whether this load breaks with a full-time job is assumed.
fix: Freeze the rules for launch and keep a one-page ops list for the job period.

title: Anyone can drain the monthly Claude allowance in a day, and every unpriced item then gets a broad guess
evidence: RANGE_ASK_DEFAULT_MONTHLY_CAP = 1000 (app/src/catalogue-first.ts:150); per-network limit 250 a day per /24 (app/server.ts:948); device ids are made up by the phone; answers are cached per product, so asking different products from 4 networks uses the month in one day. Cost per ask is about 0.23 US cents (app/src/model-cost.ts:22), so the whole cap is about US$2.30. Whether the Mac overrides the default was not visible. Attack not run.
fix: Raise the cap to a dollar budget (for example US$50 a month), count asks only from proven devices, and alarm at half.

title: Fake shopper prices poison verdicts for products Pexi has no price for
evidence: Terms s.5 and the listing: a typed price feeds other shoppers' answers. app/src/shopper-contribution.ts header: 'A product with neither has no centre, so nothing is guarded.' About 73% of scans have no shop price (NOW.md). Device ids are made up by the phone; 150 free scans an address a day (app/src/rate-limit.ts:172). Read in code, not exercised.
fix: Require two independent devices on different networks before a shopper price drives a verdict where there is no other price, and tie trust to Apple App Attest.

title: The public health page tells an attacker when Pexi is weak
evidence: Live /api/health with no token returns the Mac's battery state, failing jobs, the Claude cap state and data freshness.
fix: Answer ok or not ok publicly; put the detail behind the admin token.

title: Someone takes the Pexi name or domain after launch
evidence: RULINGS 'Name: Pexi': no trademark filed ('CIPO draft 3044038 left unsubmitted'), PEXIL pending in class 42. getpexi.app, matching the app id com.getpexi.app, is unregistered (registry RDAP 404, 2026-11-21).
fix: Buy getpexi.app now; file the CIPO mark once revenue justifies the CA$491.

title: Free incumbents with real store prices win the comparison
evidence: Assumed, not fetched: flyer and store apps in Canada show current store prices for free; docs/competitor-scanners-2026-09-19.md names Flipp and Basket but compares open-source scanners, not these.
fix: Lead the store page and first run with what they lack: a verdict for any barcode across stores in one tap.

title: Firebase launch checklist: no device attestation, so free limits key on an id the phone invents
evidence: Firebase launch checklist: 'Start enforcing Firebase App Check' to stop abuse. Pexi has no App Attest or DeviceCheck; app/src/scan-quota.ts: 'Clearing site data ... mints a new id and a fresh week'; app/src/rate-limit.ts calls the address ceiling 'what a new id cannot reset'.
fix: Add Apple App Attest on the iPhone and bind the device id to it.

title: Firebase launch checklist: quotas sized for a beta, not for launch traffic
evidence: Firebase launch checklist: 'Make sure you don't hit usage limits and quotas after going to production.' Pexi caps: 1,000 Claude range asks and 300 pack reads a month (docs/paywall-go-live-2026-11-17.md, Stop conditions). At 73% unpriced scans, a few hundred weekly users would pass 1,000 asks (assumed arithmetic, no traffic forecast exists).
fix: Resize every monthly cap from a launch traffic guess and the per-call cost, with an alarm at half.

title: Apple submission page: accessibility support is not declared
evidence: Apple's submitting page: 'Indicate your accessibility support,' such as VoiceOver and Larger Text. A grep of docs/store/listing.md for accessibility and VoiceOver found nothing.
fix: Do one VoiceOver and Larger Text pass on the main scan flow and fill the accessibility answers in App Store Connect.

title: Apple guideline 2.1 and the Firebase checklist both ask for monitoring that reaches a person; Pexi's reaches a page
evidence: Firebase checklist: members should set up 'alerts about' crashes and project state. Pexi reports problems in /api/health and a Healthchecks ping; today's live problems (failed backup, battery) are still standing. Same root as the founder-seat alarm finding.
fix: See the founder-seat alarm fix; one push channel covers both.
